newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli closure costs woman her life-minister.
newsitem.headline: Israeli closure costs woman her life-minister.

text.p: The Palestinian health minister said on Thursday a 95-year-old Gazan woman died of a blood clot because she, like others, could not get past Israeli roadblocks for hospital care.
Israel closed its borders to Palestinians and confined them to their home towns in the West Bank and Gaza Strip after a twin suicide bombing killed 13 people in a Jerusalem market eight days ago.
"I wonder how Jews who suffered collective punishment from the Nazis can practise such punishments on the Palestinian people," said Health Minister Riyad al-Zaanoun.
He said the woman, Kamleh Abu Shanab, should have been taken to a hospital in Arab East Jerusalem but could not obtain Israeli permission.
"Kamleh Abu Shanab was supposed to be transferred six days ago to Makassed Hospital but was never granted a permit and died," the health minister told a Gaza news conference.
Zaanoun said the woman, who died on Tuesday of a blood clot at age 95, was one of five people to die for lack of help but he offered no further evidence.

An Israeli spokesperson said the army lacked details. An Israeli military official said Israel would allow the transfer of about 20 truckloads of food, medicine, animal feed and other essentials into Gaza on Friday.
The health minister said patients in need of treatment at hospitals in Jerusalem, Cairo and Amman had been barred from travelling.

"Critical cases that were supposed to be transferred, such as heart surgeries and cancer tumours, exceed 80 cases...Israel claimed, for propaganda purposes, that they will absorb these cases," Zaanoun said.
"We submitted to them 60 cases and only 17 were absorbed."
When it imposed the closure following the attack, the army said entry would be allowed in medical emergencies and for medical personnel in East Jerusalem.
Zaanoun said Israel had offered Palestinian health ministry doctors permits to go to hospitals, "but we've rejected this because we don't take permits from a foreign side to move in our land".

The Union of Palestinian Medical Relief Committees said that "approximately 100 Palestinians in need of kidney dialysis were blocked from reaching hospitals". It said a woman barred from leaving Gaza could not get emergency surgery in Egypt for a brain haemorrhage.
"Pregnant women can't leave their villages to go to hospitals in West Bank cities," Zaanoun said.

"Medical teams, doctors and staff cannot reach hospitals and clinics. And shortage of medical supplies such as oxygen and medical gases, where the central storage is in Ramallah...this whole distribution system is blocked by the Israelis."
Zanoun said the measures made it difficult to organise a polio vaccination programme for Palestinian children.

"If polio virus appears it will infect Israeli children as it will infect Palestinian children. Unfortunately for Netanyahu, the virus doesn't recognise checkpoints and jumps over soldiers' guns to reach its aim."
